h1: De Princess Hotel — a white-design boutique with some of the best beds in Udon, on a quiet central street
intro: If you want a new hotel with clean, simple design and — crucially — somewhere quiet enough to actually sleep well, while still being a few minutes from the food and malls in town, De Princess Hotel Udon Thani is a name that comes up often · It is a white-toned boutique hotel that opened in 2019 on Nittayo Road, Nong Bua, a side street away from the noise yet about a 5-minute drive from UD Town and Central Plaza · Around 70 rooms, from the 32 sqm Superior King up to a Penthouse · What reviews praise again and again is comfortable beds, spacious clean rooms and a good breakfast · From approx ฿1,300/night.

body.html: De Princess Hotel is a boutique hotel that opened in 2019, so it is still relatively new and well kept · The reason guests keep coming back is its clean, contemporary white design, which feels more like a big-city hotel than a typical provincial one · It sits on Nittayo Road, Nong Bua — a quieter side street away from the bustle, with no late-night music to disturb you, yet only about a 5-minute drive from UD Town, Central Plaza and the city's food districts · It is a well-judged location for travellers who want calm without giving up convenience.

There are around 70 rooms, from the 32 sqm Superior King up to the 45 sqm Sapphire Suite, the 54 sqm Executive Suite and the 157 sqm Penthouse · Even the entry-level room is spacious and decorated in a clean, modern style, with a fridge, flat-screen TV, work desk and a bathroom with a good, powerful shower · What reviews single out most about the rooms is the beds — many call them the most comfortable they have slept in anywhere in Thailand · TripAdvisor gives the hotel a perfect 5 for sleep quality, which reflects how well it does on beds and quiet.

"The most comfortable bed I've had in Thailand. The room was spotless, the design lovely, and the hotel is so quiet I slept right through the night · Friendly staff, plenty of parking, and just a quick drive to UD Town."

Breakfast is another point of praise · It is served buffet-style at the De Nang De restaurant from 6:30 to 10:30 · There is plenty of choice, mostly Thai and Isan dishes, and the food is done well · The caveat is that if you prefer a Western breakfast (cheese, ham, several kinds of bread), the options are thinner than you might expect · Shared facilities include an outdoor pool, a fitness centre, the De Library, a co-working corner and a generous free car park with EV charging — rare at this level — plus night-time security that makes the place feel safe.

Straight talk: De Princess suits travellers who put a good night's sleep and quiet first · It scores 9.3 from 168 reviews on Trip.com and ranks #3 of 73 hotels in Udon Thani on TripAdvisor (4.7 stars), which reflects consistent satisfaction · But there are trade-offs to know · The pool and fitness centre are quite small and basic and don't quite match the hotel's image — some reviews say the pool isn't always kept spotless · Restaurant service can be slow or get orders wrong at times · And some front-desk staff have limited English · If you are coming to make serious use of the pool and gym, this may not be the one, but if you are here to relax and sleep well, it is good value.

A tip from following the reviews: because some rooms don't isolate sound well between units, if you are a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a quieter floor or a room not adjoining others when you book · Standard Superior King rates sit around ฿1,300–฿1,900/night, rising over the cool season (Dec–Feb), the Isan high season · Compare a few platforms and choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't fixed.

honestSummary: De Princess sells great beds, clean white-design rooms and quiet on a side street in the city centre — ideal for travellers here to relax and sleep deeply · The trade-offs are a small, basic pool and gym and inconsistent restaurant service.
honestChecks: If you plan to make serious use of the pool and gym — these are small and basic here, and the pool isn't always spotless → choose a hotel that focuses on facilities if that matters most.
If you are a light sleeper or sensitive to noise — some rooms don't isolate sound well between units → ask for a quieter floor or a non-adjoining room when booking, and remind them at check-in.
If you want to walk to everything without a car — the hotel is on a side street, about a 5-minute drive or ride to the malls and markets → better suited to self-drivers or those happy to use Grab.

tips.title: Ask for a quiet floor if you sleep lightly
tips.body: Some rooms don't isolate noise well between units — if you're sensitive to sound, request a quieter floor or a non-adjoining room when you book.

tips.title: Use the free parking and EV charging
tips.body: There's a generous free car park with EV charging, ideal for self-drivers — it's a 5-minute drive into the city centre.

tips.title: Try the Thai-Isan breakfast
tips.body: The buffet does Thai and Isan dishes well; Western options are limited, so plan accordingly or find a café nearby.

tips.title: Book ahead in the cool season
tips.body: Dec–Feb is the Isan high season — rates rise and rooms fill fast, so book early and pick a free-cancellation rate.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — De Princess Hotel Udon Thani

faq.q: Where is De Princess Hotel and how do I get there?
faq.a: It is at 135/135 Mu 14, Nittayo Road, Nong Bua, in central Udon Thani, on a quiet side street · Udon Thani Train Station is about 1.4 km away · UD Town, Central Plaza and Nong Bua Market are about a 5-minute drive · Nong Prajak Park is around 10 minutes · Udon Thani Airport (UTH) is about 17 minutes · There is free parking with EV charging.

faq.q: How much does De Princess Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approximately ฿1,300/night for the 32 sqm Superior King · The Sapphire Suite (45 sqm) runs around ฿2,200, the Executive Suite (54 sqm) around ฿2,900, and the largest Penthouse (157 sqm) from around ฿6,500 · Prices vary by season and package, rising over the cool season (Dec–Feb), so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is De Princess Hotel really quiet and good for sleeping?
faq.a: Quiet and good sleep are its biggest strengths · The hotel sits on a side street with no late-night music, and many reviews call the beds the most comfortable they've had in Thailand · TripAdvisor gives it a perfect 5 for sleep quality · The caveat is that some rooms don't isolate noise well between units, so light sleepers should ask for a quieter floor when booking.

faq.q: Does De Princess Hotel have a pool and a fitness centre?
faq.a: Yes to both, but they are quite small and basic · Some reviews note the pool isn't always kept spotless and the gym has limited equipment · If you are coming to make serious use of the pool and gym, this may not be your main pick, but if you are here to relax and sleep well, they are a bonus · There is also the De Library, a co-working corner and a buffet breakfast.

faq.q: Who is De Princess Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits travellers who want a quiet, restful stay, deep sleep and a clean, new design hotel · Good for couples, families and self-drivers, thanks to free parking and EV charging · If you want to walk to malls and markets without a car, or need full pool and gym facilities, you may prefer other options in town.

faq.q: Anything to know before booking De Princess Hotel?
faq.a: Things to know: the pool and gym are small, and restaurant service can be slow or get orders wrong, while some front-desk staff have limited English · Western breakfast options are few — it's mostly Thai-Isan · Light sleepers should ask for a quieter floor · Rooms fill fast in the cool season, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation rate to be safe.
